validity.recommendation: Re-attribute this row: the Acadiana Expansion Project is a Kinder Morgan Louisiana Pipeline LLC (KMLP) project, a legally and physically separate Kinder Morgan interstate system from Tennessee Gas Pipeline Company LLC (TGP) -- not a TGP segment. Check whether GEM already tracks 'Kinder Morgan Louisiana Pipeline' as its own pipeline elsewhere before deciding whether to move this row to that entity, rename pipeline_name, or add KMLP as a new pipeline. At minimum, Operator should read 'Kinder Morgan Louisiana Pipeline LLC', not left implying Tennessee Gas Pipeline is the operating entity.
validity.researcher_notes: EXISTENCE: real and well documented -- not a phantom. The project physically exists: three new 31,900 hp Solar Titan 250 compressor units added at existing Compressor Station 760 (Acadia Parish, LA) plus piping/valve modifications at the Columbia Gulf interconnect (Evangeline Parish, LA), certificated by FERC, built, and placed in service. ATTRIBUTION PROBLEM: every independent primary source found names the owning/operating entity as 'Kinder Morgan Louisiana Pipeline LLC' (KMLP), never Tennessee Gas Pipeline. (1) FERC Order 172 FERC P 61,259, Docket CP19-484-000, issued 2020-09-17 (mirror of the official order, verified live, states 'Kinder Morgan Louisiana Pipeline LLC ... filed an application ... requesting a certificate ... (Acadiana Project)'; the applicant of record throughout the order is KMLP, never TGP). (2) EIA Today in Energy, id=50376 (in the row's own harvested citation pool, cite_note-:1-10) states verbatim: 'This 894 million cubic feet per day (MMcf/d) expansion on the Kinder Morgan Louisiana intrastate pipeline increases takeaway capacity out of the Haynesville Basin, connecting it to the Sabine Pass LNG terminal' -- and, in the SAME article, separately describes the unrelated '261 Upgrade Projects ... delivered by the Tennessee Gas Pipeline (TGP) into New England,' confirming EIA itself treats TGP and KMLP as two different systems. (3) Kinder Morgan's own KMLP tariff informational-posting site (pipeline2.kindermorgan.com, Notice ID 39680, 'RES. OF CAP. FOR EXPANSION - ACADIANA') identifies the TSP as '809611911-KM LOUISIANA PIPELINE' and the project as reserving capacity on 'KMLP's Segment 100 and 200' -- an operator disclosure, not press paraphrase. (4) Kinder Morgan Inc.'s own SEC 8-K exhibits for Q3 2021 (filed 2021-10-21) and Q4 2021 (filed 2022-01-19) both describe 'Kinder Morgan Louisiana Pipeline's ... Acadiana expansion project' as placed in service -- and the SAME Q3 2021 8-K, in an adjacent bullet, separately reports on TGP's Line 261 Upgrade in Agawam, Massachusetts and a different TGP compression project with a November 2022 target, showing KMI itself keeps TGP and KMLP as distinct reporting lines. (5) federalregister.gov's docket page for CP19-484-000 lists the applicant as 'Kinder Morgan Louisiana Pipeline LLC' across all four Federal Register notices for this docket (Notice of Application 2019-07-19, NOI 2019-09-04, Schedule Notice 2019-09-30, EA Notice 2020-02-12). (6) Reuters (2020-10-21, via Wayback since live Reuters 401s scrapers) headlines 'Kinder Morgan gets U.S. OK to start Louisiana Acadiana natgas project' and text confirms 'a unit of Kinder Morgan Inc ... permission to start construction of the company's proposed Acadiana natural gas pipeline project' -- consistent with a KMLP subsidiary, not naming TGP. Six independent origins (a FERC order, a federal statistical agency, the operator's own tariff postings, the operator's own SEC 8-Ks x2, a federal notice archive, and wire press) all agree this segment belongs to KMLP. CLASSIFICATION/SPEC checks that hold up: Fuel=Gas and PipelineType=transmission are correct (an NGA section 7(c) interstate transmission certificate). Capacity=894.00 MMcf/d is exactly right (FERC: 'an additional 894,000 dekatherms per day (Dth/d)'; EIA: '894 MMcf/d'). LengthKnown=0.00/blank Diameter is correct per the no-new-pipe convention: FERC's order confirms this is a compression-only expansion (new compressor units + auxiliary facilities at an EXISTING compressor station; no new mainline pipe). SegmentCost=143,000,000 matches the FERC-approved pre-construction estimate almost exactly ($143,048,567, FERC order P11; corroborated independently by Reuters' '$143 million') -- flagging as a caveat only: KMI's own later SEC 8-Ks give a higher in-progress estimate ($145M, Q3 2021 8-K) and then a lower final figure (~$127M, Q4 2021 8-K) as the project was actually built out; the sheet's $143M is a legitimate primary-sourced figure (the FERC estimate) but is not the final realized cost -- Baird's call whether to swap to the ~$127M actual. DID NOT independently corroborate: no second field/plant-level FuelSource beyond the general 'Haynesville Basin' EIA mention (a basin/play is not a named field/facility per the FuelSource convention), and no MAOP/Pressure figure for the compressor-only facilities in the sources read. Opened/attempted 4 of the row's 37 harvested wiki citations directly on point (kindermorgan.com Operations/Natural-Gas index -- live, general TGP page, not Acadiana-specific; eia.gov id=50376 -- live, used as source #2 above; reuters.com Acadiana article -- live via Wayback, used as source #6; gascompressionmagazine.com 'Acadiana Project Moves Forward' -- live-403's scripted clients and its Wayback capture is blocked by a JS/cookie challenge, could not read). The remaining 33 harvested citations are TGP national-system items (PHMSA incident/enforcement pages, 1960s-2010s pipeline-explosion news archives, the unrelated Northeast Energy Direct/261 Upgrade/Utica-Marcellus NGL conversion stories) that describe TGP's actual own system and are not relevant to this KMLP segment's data columns, so were not opened further. Six additional primary sources beyond the harvested pool were found via open-web search: the FERC order itself, federalregister.gov's CP19-484-000 docket page, KMLP's own tariff informational posting, naturalgasintel.com (2022-07-25), and Kinder Morgan's SEC 8-K exhibits for Q3 2021 and Q4 2021.

validity.recommendation: Correct StartYear1 from 2022 to 2021 (StartMonth1 stays 10); full in-service was 2021-10-20, not 2022.
validity.researcher_notes: The sheet's Start date (StartYear1=2022, StartMonth1=10) is materially wrong -- off by a full year. Kinder Morgan Inc.'s own SEC 8-K exhibit for Q3 2021 (filed 2021-10-21, covering the quarter through Sept 2021) states: 'Kinder Morgan Louisiana Pipeline's approximately $145 million Acadiana expansion project began partial service on October 1, 2021, with full in-service expected in the fourth quarter of 2021, ahead of schedule.' The follow-on Q4 2021 8-K (filed 2022-01-19) confirms completion: 'Kinder Morgan Louisiana Pipeline's approximately $127 million Acadiana expansion project was placed in full service on October 20, 2021, ahead of schedule.' Both are official SEC-filed operator disclosures, filed three months apart, and independently corroborated by EIA's Today in Energy (2021-11-17): 'The Acadiana Expansion Project, partly completed as of August 6, 2021 ... expected to be completed in early 2022' -- consistent with a partial-service Oct 1 2021 / full-service Oct 20 2021 timeline that EIA's forward-looking Nov 2021 language (written before the Jan 2022 8-K confirmed the actual date) slightly underestimated. No source found anywhere -- including a targeted search for an October 2022 completion -- supports a 2022 in-service date; a Reuters piece (2020-10-21) and Kinder Morgan's own January 2019 open-season notice both gave EARLIER target estimates (Q2 2022 / 'as early as Feb 1, 2022') that were themselves superseded by the actual ahead-of-schedule 2021 completion. See the proposed fills[] object for the corrected value.

summary: P2497 (Tennessee Gas Pipeline / Acadiana Expansion Project) exists and is correctly operating/transmission/gas, but is misattributed: six independent primary sources (FERC order CP19-484-000, EIA, Kinder Morgan's own KMLP tariff postings, two KMI SEC 8-Ks, federalregister.gov) show this is a Kinder Morgan LOUISIANA Pipeline LLC project, not Tennessee Gas Pipeline -- filed as attribution concern with a recommendation to re-home the row. Also caught a one-year Start-date error (sheet says 2022; KMI's own 8-Ks put full in-service at 2021-10-20) -- filed as a spec concern with a corrected fills[] value. Capacity (894 MMcf/d), Length=0/no Diameter (compression-only, no new pipe), Fuel, PipelineType, SegmentCost ($143M, matches the FERC estimate) all confirmed. Filled Proposal (2019-06), Construction (2020, quarter only), and the blank Start/End states (Louisiana/Louisiana). Left Pressure, Diameter, and FuelSource UNRESOLVED/blank (no sourced value found, or intentionally blank per convention). No plausible duplicate found in the 37-row roster (Kinder Morgan Louisiana Pipeline is not one of the other 36 names).
